sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (National Jurisdiction, Panama City Registry District)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) core with Anglo-American-inspired corporate and trust-like foundation statutes imported by Ley 25 de 1995
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States - Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 11 May 1991)
United States - Panama Trade Promotion Agreement / FTA (in force 31 October 2012)
Tax Information Exchange Agreements in force with OECD member states under the Panama-OECD TIEA framework
Double Taxation Agreements in force with the Republic of Korea, United Arab Emirates, and Mexico (limited income coverage)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama AML/CFT Framework Law) as amended; Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law); Ley 52 de 2016 and Executive Decree No. 163 de 2020 (Sole Registry of Final Beneficiaries - RUBF); implementing UAF (Unidad de Analisis Financiero) resolutions and FATF-aligned supervisory directives of the Registro Publico de Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the founder's passport (bio-data page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or civil identification authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (if the origin state is a Hague Apostille Convention party); otherwise consular legalization at a Panamanian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter covering the founder and all foundation council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed original with notarized signature; Apostille or consular legalization where required by the issuing jurisdiction's notarial practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of founder (recent utility bill or bank statement, not older than 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or licensed commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy bearing seal/signature; Apostille generally waived when certified by a notary of an Apostille state; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of the corporate founder (if the founder is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or chamber of commerce of the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registry-certified copy with Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the resident agent and registration signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian notary public (if executed in Panama) or foreign notary plus Apostille (if executed abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus sworn Spanish translation; prevailing practice permits execution before a Panamanian notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening per Ley 23/2015, UAF directives and FATF Recommendations 12: positive-match screening against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UK HMT, and the national Panamanian UAF watchlist; all natural persons owning 25% or more (or otherwise exercising control) must be identified and verified; PEPs, PEP family members and close associates trigger enhanced due diligence with documented source of wealth and source of funds; ongoing transaction monitoring applies, including card-network and Stripe/PayPal UBO re-verification obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Sede Electronica (electronic name search and non-registration certificate service, Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be formulated in Spanish or any Latin-script language. The registered name must incorporate or end with the statutory designation 'Fundacion de Interes Privado' (PIF). Transliterations must not render the name identical or phonetically confusing with any existing registered entity; accents and punctuation are harmonized for the alphabetical index of the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within ten (10) business days of receipt of the rejection notice, the applicant through a duly licensed Panamanian attorney may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideracion y Apelacion en subsidio' before the Direccion General of the Registro Publico de Panama; the motion must be drafted in Spanish, must allege prior-right or material registry error, and must annex the preliminary non-registration search certificate; alternatively, the applicant may obtain a fresh fee-based name reservation and resubmit the same name with a distinctive prefix, suffix or transliteration variation; a favorable appellate resolution is typically issued within 15 to 20 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the statutory registered office: every Private Interest Foundation must appoint a licensed resident agent maintaining a physical office in Panama where the foundation's statutory books and UBO records are kept. The online-only e-commerce activity under ISIC 4791 requires no physical trading premises in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low statistical risk (below 10% annual probability for a low-risk online retail foundation with compliant substance), but the Registro Publico and the UAF may conduct unannounced inspections of the resident agent's books where payment-rail terminations, customer complaints, or PEP/sanction indicators arise; resident agent must produce UBO records and foundation ledger within 72 hours.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry name search and non-registration certificate (Fundaciones de Interes Privado section)
Foundation incorporation legal fees (drafting of acta constitutiva, reglamento interno, foundation council minutes and due-diligence legal opinion)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm / resident agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial capital endowment (patrimonio inicial) of the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foundation treasury (statutory minimum capital of the PIF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customary minimum capital requirement under Ley 25/1995

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the foundation charter and supporting instruments before a Panamanian notary
Apostille and authentication fees for founder documents (estimated two documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Cancilleria de Panama)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per apostille (approx. USD 40 - 60 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry inscription and annotation fee (Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff based on foundation duration (commonly 50-year term)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent fee and registered office provision (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent / corporate services provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing with the Sole Registry of Final Beneficiaries (RUBF) under Ley 52/2016
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos / Registro Publico de Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC and PEP/sanctions screening for founder, foundation council and protector (if any)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk standard screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Document courier, Spanish translation and legalization handling contingency

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Law No. 32 of 2013 (registered-agent beneficial ownership recordkeeping) and related transparency decrees; operative sections include Article 5 (minimum endowment), Articles 6 and 7 (registered agent and registered office), and Articles 10 to 13 (Foundation Council and Protector clauses).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Registration Department)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarized Public Deed of Constitution of a Private Interest Foundation), protocolized in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Article 5 of Law 25/1995 requires an initial endowment of no less than USD 10,000 (B/.10,000.00) or its equivalent in another currency, which may be contributed in cash, securities, or in-kind assets at the date of constitution and must be formally attested to the Resident Agent; Panamanian law does not mandate an escrow or blocked account for this endowment. The annual foundation tax of USD 300 (Law 25/1995 fee schedule) is payable for each calendar year and must be settled before the Registry issues the inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Founder subscribes the initial endowment of USD 10,000, in accordance with Article 5 of Law 25 of June 12, 1995, as amended, and ratifies the Foundation Charter registered at the Public Registry of Panama. RESOLVED, that the registered office and licensed Resident Agent are established at the Resident Agency's Panama City address. RESOLVED, that the Foundation Council is appointed: [President], [Secretary], [Treasurer], each accepting three-year terms. RESOLVED, that the Council is authorized to open bank accounts, appoint a Protector, and execute all instruments to pursue the Foundation's objective of internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment and online payment processing through Stripe and PayPal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile and Foundations Information Desk (conducted through a licensed Panamanian attorney)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed resident agent to run a name-eligibility search at the Public Registry; for private interest foundations there is no formal pre-reservation certificate, so the attorney verifies absence of identical or deceptively similar registered entity names and confirms that the selected name includes the lawful suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or acceptable equivalent. The attorney then fixes the preferred name for the notarial protocolization window.
required_dossiers: At least three foundation name variants in Spanish or acceptable foreign language
Certified passport copy of the Founder/Settlor
Written attorney instruction letter and power of attorney (poder)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or notary identifies a conflicting registered name, file substitute name alternatives or obtain a written consent letter from the prior registered entity; if the conflict persists, select the next available name and re-execute the charter before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Notary of the Judicial Circuit of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Settlor, personally or through an empowered attorney, executes the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the mandatory Law 25/1995 clauses: foundation name, lawful object (internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping equipment), registered office, initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, the Foundation Council members with their identifying data, the beneficiary determination rules, optional Protector appointment, and adoption of the Reglamento (foundation regulations). The notary authenticates signatures and issues the 'primer testimonio' (first notarial exemplar) and certified copies for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Draft Escritura Pública (Foundation Charter)
Reglamento / Foundation Regulations (internal bylaws)
Notarized power of attorney if the Founder does not appear personally
Certified passport copies of the Founder and all Foundation Council members
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank reference) for each officer
AML/KYC questionnaire executed by the Founder and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to incomplete clauses (for example, object, endowment, or beneficiary rules), amend the draft and re-execute the deed; if the final endowment or name changes, recalculate and pay the supplemental stamp fees before protocolization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of annual foundation tax and registry stamp fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Banco Nacional de Panamá (revenue windows); Tesorería del Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the USD 300 annual foundation tax (Law 25/1995 fee schedule) for the calendar year of incorporation using the official tax payment form at a designated bank window or the DGI collection platform; concurrently pay the Public Registry inscription fees calculated on the endowment value (estimated USD 350 for the standard USD 10,000 endowment). Obtain the bank receipt and treasury stamps ('timbres fiscales') which must be annexed to the registry application.
required_dossiers: Foundation tax payment form (declaración/cédula de pago)
Bank deposit receipt issued by Banco Nacional de Panamá or authorized collection bank
Registry stamp fee calculation sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied or duplicated, request a written 'certificación de pago' from DGI or the Treasury, reconcile the amounts, and obtain a corrected stamped receipt before filing with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation at the Public Registry (Inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'solicitud de inscripción' in Spanish attaching the first notarial testimonio of the Escritura, the registered agent acceptance letter, and the official fee receipts. The Registry conducts the legal qualification review ('calificación registral') of the foundation acts, verifying lawful name, legal object, minimum endowment, appointment of the Panama Resident Agent, and conformity with Law 25/1995. Upon approval, the Registry issues the inscription order assigning the foundation registration number and 'ficha registral', thereby creating the foundation as a juridical person.
required_dossiers: First notarial testimonio of the Escritura Pública (certified or apostilled as appropriate)
Power of attorney of the filing attorney and copy of the attorney's professional credential
Registered Agent acceptance letter (carta de aceptación del agente residente)
Foundation tax and registry stamp fee receipts
Certified copy of the notary authorization if execution was by mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect memorandum ('defecto') or negative qualification, the attorney files a cure ('subsanación') within 10 business days by adding the missing clause or document; if the rejection is substantive, re-execute the charter before the notary, pay any supplemental stamp fees, and file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Registration Certificate and Resident Agent Custody File
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Centro de Certificaciones y Copias; licensed Resident Agent (Panamanian attorney)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order the official 'Certificado de Inscripción y Existencia de la Fundación' and certified copy of the 'ficha registral' from the Registry's certification office, noting the certificate's limited validity period. The licensed Resident Agent thereafter opens and maintains the Law 32/2013 custody file containing the factual beneficial-ownership records of the Foundation (Founder, Council members, Protector, and beneficiaries) and confirms continuous compliance with the registered-agent duty under Law 25/1995.
required_dossiers: Certified-copy request form completed before the Registry
Ficha registral reference number of the registered foundation
Payment receipt for certification fees
Law 32/2013 beneficial ownership forms completed through the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified data contain discrepancies (for example, name spelling or date errors), file a request for 'anotación de aclaratoria' at the Registry before relying on the certificate; if the custody file is incomplete, immediately complete the missing Law 32/2013 declarations with the Resident Agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Council Organizational Meeting, Statutory Books, and Digital Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación) acting with the licensed Resident Agent's law office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council in person or by unanimous written consent and adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Record the minutes in Spanish and open the four statutory books required by Panamanian practice for foundations: Registro de Fundadores (Founders' Register), Registro del Consejo de la Fundación (Council Register), Registro de Beneficiarios (Beneficiaries' Register), and Libro de Actas y Resoluciones (Minutes and Resolutions Book). These books remain private records, not filed with the Registry, but must be produced to Panamanian authorities upon lawful request.
required_dossiers: Signed Pro-Forma First Board Resolution text
Certified passport copies and notarized signatures of Council members
Written acceptance letters of each Council member
Proof of registered office address (lease or consent of the Resident Agent)
Statutory book templates or certified digital ledger format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes or books are challenged by courts or regulators, the Council ratifies the records in a supplementary formal meeting with notarial attestation and, where necessary, renumbers and re-dates the minutes with the Resident Agent's certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and municipal operating registration for e-commerce activity (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas y Oficinas de Avisos de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) identifying the Foundation as the online merchant and, where applicable, as importer of record for outdoor camping equipment; file the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' application covering the digital retail establishment and pay the municipal fee based on estimated turnover. No prior industrial or manufacturing license is required from MICI for ISIC 4791 pure online retail; the municipal Aviso de Operación serves as the operating permit enabling invoicing and payment-processing platform onboarding. If annual taxable turnover exceeds the electronic-invoicing threshold, enroll in the DGI e-invoicing system.
required_dossiers: Foundation registration certificate (Ficha) and certificate of good standing
RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
Passports or national IDs of the Administrator and Foundation Council members
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Lease or ownership title evidencing the registered operating address
Copies of payment-rail contracts (Stripe/PayPal) if already executed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality attempts to classify the activity under industrial or manufacturing categories, file a written reclassification petition citing ISIC 4791 and NAICS 459110 and the purely digital nature of the business; if DGI questions the merchant type, provide the Foundation charter's e-commerce object clause and the Stripe/PayPal merchant identification documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Comercio Interior; no industrial manufacturing license applies to ISIC 4791 pure online retailing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Permiso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Operation Notice) issued by the Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá; optional Patente de Comercio registration only if a physical sales premise other than the registered office is established

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (formerly ANAM)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category I (non-threatening activity): ISIC 4791 online retail without manufacturing requires neither a full EIA report nor an EIA registration; the operator may request a 'Certificado de No Requerimiento de Estudio de Impacto Ambiental' for record. If a fulfillment warehouse exceeding office scale is opened, a Category II simplified EIA screening will apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or VOC emission points exist in pure e-commerce operations. Compliance triggers: (i) sanitary wastewater from the registered office and any warehouse connected to municipal sewerage must meet the national recipient-body discharge parameters of Resolución AG-0372-2013 (as amended by MiAMBIENTE), including pH 6-9, BOD5 and TSS limitations applicable to urban commercial establishments; (ii) solid waste management under Law 33 of 2018 (Ley General de Gestión Integral de Residuos), covering recyclable packaging and returned-product e-waste disposal through authorized haulers; (iii) no VOC threshold applies because no coating, printing, adhesive, or solvent processing operations are conducted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the registered office and any storage space (exits, extinguishers, smoke detection, and means of escape); occupational safety clearance by the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) covering the workplace risk-prevention program and workstation ergonomics; structural and land-use inspection ('certificado de uso de suelo y construcción') from the Alcaldía de Panamá if additional shelving or mezzanine loads exceed ordinary office loads; and emergency-plan acknowledgment from SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil) for any warehouse area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Primary electronic portal: SAG (Sistema de Administración de Gestión) at https://sag.mef.gob.pa; additional e-filing and ITBMS services at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney and appoint a resident fiscal representative if the foundation council is non-resident. (2) Execute and register the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) charter (pacto constitutivo/fundacional) with the Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) and obtain the foundation registration certificate. (3) File Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) with the DGI, attaching the public deed, foundation charter, registration certificate, and notarized passports of foundation council members. (4) Obtain the RUC certificate (Aviso de Inscripción). (5) Apply for ITBMS activation if the PIF will engage in taxable supplies of goods or services. (6) Activate the SAG e-Tax account and digital signature for electronic submissions. Expected completion: 5-15 business days; no personal appearance by foreign founders is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope. The PIF is a distinct juridical person taxed only on Panama-source income; foreign-source income, including Internet retail revenue from customers abroad where title and delivery occur outside Panama, remains outside the territorial income tax net. The PIF is not pass-through eligible for DGI purposes; net Panama-source income is taxed at the entity level, while benefits distributed to non-resident beneficiaries generally do not constitute Panama-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Panama. Available mechanisms include: (i) reservation of founder powers (to revoke, amend, or designate beneficiaries) expressly inserted into the PIF charter under Law 25 of 1995, determining segregation of foundation assets; (ii) voluntary registration as a small taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) under the simplified ITBMS regime for annual gross receipts not exceeding B/. 36,000; (iii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) election under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying regional service income; (iv) hybrid instrument and financial arrangement documentation elections under Law 7 of 2019 implementing OECD BEPS Action 2. All elections are formal filings with the DGI or Public Registry rather than annual elective classification forms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian value added tax applicable to transfers of movable property and supplies of services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All persons habitually carrying out taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS before commencing activities; there is no general numeric annual exemption from registration. The simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Simplificado de Pequeño Contribuyente) applies to businesses with annual gross receipts of B/. 36,000 or less (PAB equivalent of USD 36,000), permitting quarterly simplified filing. For foreign e-commerce sellers, any sale with delivery to a Panamanian address creates ITBMS registration nexus from the first sale; no de minimis distance-selling threshold exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) administered by the DGI through the SAG platform. Registered ITBMS taxpayers must: (i) obtain certification from an authorized electronic invoicing service provider (PSFE) or certify an in-house system; (ii) issue invoices in DGI-compliant XML/JSON formats, incorporating the cryptographic digital seal (Firma Digital); (iii) transmit each invoice to the DGI for near-real-time fiscal validation before delivery to the customer; (iv) use electronic credit/debit notes under the same sealing and clearance rules. Integration is performed via documented SOAP/REST APIs with the PSFE or direct SAG endpoints. DGI Resolution No. 201-8690 phased in mandatory use by taxpayer category; invoices lacking DGI clearance are treated as not issued, thereby disallowing input tax credits and export zero-rating. No separate adhesive fiscal stamp is required beyond the DGI digital seal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to exports of tangible goods physically leaving Panamanian customs territory, to supplies into qualifying free zones (e.g., Zona Libre de Colón), and to services rendered to non-resident beneficiaries where use or exploitation occurs abroad. Eligibility requires: (i) active DGI ITBMS registration; (ii) a valid export customs declaration (DUE - Declaración Única de Exportación) accepted by the National Customs Authority; (iii) issuance of the commercial invoice through the e-invoicing system with explicit zero-rated annotation; (iv) retention of transport documents proving physical departure; (v) for Internet retail, the goods must be dispatched to a non-Panamanian delivery address and must leave Panamanian territory, otherwise the 7% rate applies; e-commerce operators must separately identify domestic and export sales in ITBMS periodic returns to support refunds or credit carry-forward.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUE - Declaración Única de Exportación) accepted and validated by the National Customs Authority (ANA)
Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque) or Air Waybill evidencing departure from Panamanian territory
Commercial invoice with zero-rated ITBMS annotation
Proof of foreign delivery (courier tracking record or proof of delivery from the foreign carrier)
Inward remittance certificate or bank statement evidencing the foreign payment (Comprobante de Remesa del Exterior)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exports zero-rated without valid export documentation are reclassified as domestic taxable sales; the DGI will assess the unpaid 7% ITBMS plus late-payment interest under Article 731 of the Código Fiscal and impose fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the omitted tax for fraudulent conduct under Articles 750 et seq. of the Código Fiscal. Failure in digital e-invoice clearance automatically disqualifies the export exemption for the relevant tax period. Criminal tax evasion under Law 70 of 2019 exposes founders and foundation council members to imprisonment, ineligibility, and disqualification; the DGI may suspend the foundation's tax registration and revoke its e-invoicing certification. Retrospective clawback periods extend to five years, and are indefinite in cases involving fraud or forgery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama operates without a central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established under Decree Law 9 of 26 February 1998 (as amended), is the autonomous banking and financial system regulator. Banco Nacional de Panamá, a 100% state-owned commercial bank, acts as fiscal agent for the State but holds no monetary-issue, lender-of-last-resort, or FX-intervention powers. The U.S. Dollar is legal tender under Article 184 of the Political Constitution of Panama, creating a fully dollarized monetary regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa (PAB) exists only as divisional coins fixed at 1:1 with the USD; no paper balboas are issued. The capital and current accounts are fully open: no exchange control laws, no convertibility approvals, no quota systems, and no surrender requirements apply to any currency. Profit remittances, foundation distributions, redemption of beneficiary interests, and capital repatriation by non-residents are unrestricted and, under Panama's territorial tax system, are not taxed unless the income source is Panamanian. Foreign currencies (EUR, GBP, CNY) may be freely held, converted, or exported through commercial clearing at market rates without central-bank consent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no notification duty for export proceeds, e-commerce receipts, or other trade balances. Receipts may remain indefinitely in foreign bank accounts; the SBP only applies anti-money-laundering reporting to unusual transactions under Law 23 of 27 April 2015. For the ISIC 4791 internet-retail model, Stripe/PayPal settlements may be accumulated offshore and wired to the PIF account on the foundation's own treasury calendar without conversion mandates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD checking) and segregated Collections Sub-Account
Capital Escrow Account (segregated term deposit) and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for Panama-domiciled EMIs; Panama does not issue a dedicated electronic-money-institution license, and non-bank payment operators must be registered with the SBP. Major offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Airwallex) do not generally onboard Panamanian Private Interest Foundations. PayPal accepts Panamanian business registrations for receiving funds, but Stripe does not list Panama as a supported merchant market. The practical structure is an intermediate merchant-of-record (e.g., a U.S. LLC or licensed PSP gateway) executing card-not-present acquiring, with settlement flows wired onward to the Panamanian PIF account under documented agreements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, most Tier-1 Panamanian banks require the settlor and at least one nominated council member (Patronato) to attend an in-person onboarding interview at a Panamanian branch for a Private Interest Foundation. Remote opening is tolerated only when a regulated correspondent bank, Panamanian law firm, or licensed trustee introduces the client under a documented KYC certificate with all signatures notarized and apostilled (Hague Convention, ratified by Panama). SBP rules do not statutorily mandate face-to-face identity verification, but banks apply an internal 'know your client in person' standard for foreign UBOs of foundation structures; no consular alternative exists. Budget 5-10 business days for identity verification and dossier review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structure opacity: layered PIF with undefined or reserved beneficiaries and no declared economic purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter and Reglamento (bylaws) filed in the Public Registry; full ledger of initial and reserved beneficiaries; passport copies and professional references of all council members; sworn declaration of intended e-commerce activity; reference letter from a licensed Panamanian law firm or registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable e-commerce revenue: high-volume, small-ticket card payments flowing from Stripe/PayPal without reconciliation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor settlement statements with batch-level hash; PayPal/Stripe transaction-level CSV exports reconciled to bank credits; supplier contracts; shipping and customs manifests; inventory ownership records; and a profit-and-loss summary prepared by a licensed Panamanian CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid round-tripping: funds credited and immediately redirected to private beneficiaries or third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual financial statements of the foundation; minutes of council resolutions authorizing each disbursement; commercial-purpose evidence (sales invoices, supplier purchase orders); and a cash-flow forecast showing the 30-60 day inventory cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or beneficiaries domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions-screening results (World-Check / UN / OFAC); source-of-wealth letters from regulated banks in the UBO's home jurisdiction; tax-residence certificates; passport and proof-of-address for every beneficiary and council member.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent switching of payment rails or atypical clearing paths inconsistent with the declared retail business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe/PayPal or the intermediate PSP; payout schedule documentation; and a treasury policy memorandum, pre-approved by the Bank, describing inbound and outbound clearing routes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Settlor capital injection: route via SWIFT MT103 in USD with the beneficiary field exactly matching the registered foundation name plus 'Fundación de Interés Privado' suffix; the remittance information should read 'Capital contribution - foundation initial endowment.' Panama maintains no statutory purpose-code table; the free-text remittance field is determinative. For U.S.-origin funds, credit via Fedwire or ACH to the Panamanian bank's U.S. correspondent (Citibank N.A., JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A., Bank of America N.A., or Wells Fargo Bank N.A.), then onward SWIFT credit to the PIF account. The injected capital must equal or exceed the amount stated in the Foundation Charter and Public Registry filing (commonly USD 10,000; lower amounts may trigger enhanced SBP value reporting). Verification bundle: (1) notarized source-of-funds declaration executed by the settlor within 30 days; (2) statement proving ownership of the external funding account; (3) the registered Charter; (4) foundation council minutes ratifying account opening. PSP settlements from PayPal or the intermediate Stripe gateway should be credited only to the dedicated collections sub-account, and each settlement batch must reconcile to the PSP payout report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for inventory purchases: use SWIFT MT103 with tags 50K (ordering customer) and 59 (supplier) referencing genuine invoices; larger or recurring orders may be supported by irrevocable documentary letters of credit confirmed by the supplier's bank. Domestic logistics, warehousing, and utility payments clear through Panama's Automated Clearing House (ACH) operated by the banking community under SBP oversight. Structural note: for the ISIC 4791 model, Stripe does not support Panama-domiciled merchants and PayPal Panama support is limited to receiving; therefore an intermediate merchant-of-record entity executes card-not-present acquiring. Payouts from that entity to the PIF must be documented under a merchant-of-record agreement, with the intermediate entity's audited settlement statements attached to each inward credit to prevent mischaracterization as unrelated third-party flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards on EUR/USD and GBP/USD executed via the offshore trading desks of SBP-licensed international banks
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in USD for Chinese supplier exposures
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and USD/CNH) for notional amounts above USD 1 million with maturities beyond 12 months
Vanilla European-style FX call and put options for cash-flow-contingent foreign-currency inventory purchases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas - Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory surcharge and interest accrue during delinquency; continued non-payment results in administrative suspension, loss of good standing, and eventual strike-off from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ultimate Beneficial Owner Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each annual registration anniversary; any substantial ownership change must be updated within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines per Panama's UBO regulations; repeated non-filing or false filing may suspend the foundation's legal good standing and active status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Agent Annual Compliance Review and Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct government filing; confirmation maintained by the licensed resident agent and made available to the Public Registry upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the foundation's formation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent subjects the foundation to administrative dissolution; agent resignation without timely replacement leads to strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Public Interest Foundations (PIFs) are not subject to a compulsory audit solely as legal vehicles. If the foundation engages in commercial retail activity and its Panamanian-source gross income exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 1,000,000, it must file audited financial statements with the DGI. Otherwise audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is mandated for a dormant PIF. Where books are prepared, IFRS or Panamanian GAAP (Código Fiscal and NICCF) may be adopted; tax filings follow the Territorial Tax Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Within 30 days after each anniversary, the foundation council must deliver to the resident agent a written representation confirming the current settlor, foundation council members, protector (if any), and beneficiaries. Any change in the shareholding or beneficial-ownership structure must be reported to the resident agent within 30 days, who maintains the UBO registry and fulfills DGI reporting requirements.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 950 - 2,500 per year depending on agent and compliance complexity
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit for dormant vehicle; voluntary audit USD 2,500 - 5,000 for an active e-commerce PIF

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on the basis of Panamanian-source net income (territorial taxation); no tax on foreign-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with no Panamanian-source commercial activity, effective income tax is zero. Statutory incentives include the territorial exclusion for foreign-source e-commerce revenue, statutory exemption for capital gains derived from assets located outside Panama, and the availability of a 5-year net operating loss carryforward for losses incurred in Panamanian-source operations. There are no general tax holidays; the principal advantage is the complete exclusion of offshore internet retail income from the 25% headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 20 - Declaracion Jurada Anual de Impuesto Sobre la Renta (Personas Juridicas), filed electronically through the Direccion General de Ingresos e-Tax platform (dgi.mef.gob.pa) using an RUC and qualified digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a nil return is required only when the PIF is registered with the DGI as an income-tax taxpayer but has no Panamanian-source income. A purely passive PIF that engages in no Panamanian-source activity is not obliged to file Form 20 and owes only the annual Public Registry foundation fee.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than March 31 of the calendar year immediately following the close of the tax period for entities on the calendar year; for entities with a DGI-approved non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Unico de Contribuyente assigned by the DGI upon taxpayer registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the foundation's RUC when registered. A non-resident-owned PIF must obtain a local RUC only if it engages in Panamanian-source activity; otherwise no Form 20 is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The tax period reported, normally 01/01/2024 to 12/31/2024.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foundation's adopted fiscal year as stated in its charter; the default is the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Panamanian-source activities such as retail sales in Panama, local services, or the use of intangible property in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border internet sales of outdoor camping equipment where the seller, warehouse, and fulfillment activities are outside Panama, report zero unless the PIF has a permanent establishment, local inventory, or delivery personnel in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue derived from sources outside Panama and excluded under the territorial tax system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Stripe and PayPal proceeds attributable to shipments from abroad and foreign fulfillment operations as foreign-source income. Maintain logistics contracts, shipment records, and payment-provider statements in the tax file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred to obtain Panamanian-source taxable income, allowable under Articles 55 through 61 of the Codigo Fiscal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct foreign e-commerce marketing, hosting, or fulfillment expenses against a nil Panamanian-source position. If any Panamanian-source income exists, allocate expenses using arm's-length, documented cost allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after deductions, exemptions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for a purely offshore PIF. Retain board minutes confirming the absence of Panamanian-source operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Impuesto a la Renta Calculado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The statutory 25% entity-level tax on Line 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero when Line 6 is zero. If Panamanian-source activity exists, compute 25% of the taxable net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 - Pagos a Cuenta y Retenciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments and taxes withheld by clients, contribution accounts, or payment processors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any 2% withholding applied by Panamanian buyers and monthly advance payments. A non-resident PIF will normally enter zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 9 - Impuesto por Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after prepayments and credits, or a refundable balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero-fill for the offshore PIF. Any due tax must be paid through the DGI e-Tax platform using Panamanian banking rails, never directly through Stripe or PayPal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualified electronic signature of the legal representative, resident agent, or registered accountant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF's registered director or resident agent must execute the return. If the director is outside Panama, execute a notarized tax power of attorney and follow the DGI remote signature protocol.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge equal to 10% of the tax due (minimum B/.50), monthly moratory interest on unpaid tax at the statutory rate set by the DGI, and possible inclusion in the public list of taxpayers in arrears. Persistent non-filing permits DGI tax assessment by omission, suspension of the foundation's taxpayer ID, and rejection of subsequent permits or banking applications.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions to non-resident shareholders or beneficiaries, reduced to 5% when the distribution is made out of profits that have already borne the 25% corporate income tax. Distributions by a PIF of foreign-source assets or foreign-source e-commerce profits are not Panamanian-source income and are outside the Panamanian dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (DTA), the payee must obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from the treaty-jurisdiction revenue authority, confirm beneficial ownership of the income, submit the treaty-relief declaration electronically to the DGI, and provide the Panamanian withholding agent with a completed Form 22 or equivalent before payment. A PIF can only claim treaty benefits if it is itself a Panamanian tax resident under the integrated resident-liable-to-tax test and has sufficient economic substance under Law 254 of 2021; a fully tax-exempt foundation will ordinarily be denied DTA relief under limitation-of-benefits clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid for the use of trademarks, software, or industrial rights in Panama are subject to a statutory 12.5% withholding tax; DTA rates typically range from 5% to 10%. Cross-border interest paid by a Panamanian debtor to a non-resident creditor is subject to a 5% withholding tax unless the creditor is a licensed Panamanian bank or a treaty resident entitled to a reduced rate. Interest earned on funds held by the PIF outside Panama and paid by foreign borrowers is foreign-source income and not subject to Panamanian withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is required where related-party transactions in a tax year exceed B/.250,000 (USD 250,000). This includes purchases of camping equipment from affiliated suppliers, brand licensing fees, management fees, or loans with related parties. Taxpayers must also file the annual transfer-pricing information affidavit with the DGI when related-party transactions exceed the same threshold; group entities meeting the consolidated revenue threshold must submit a Country-by-Country report notification.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - Comparable Uncontrolled Price method for commodity-type camping gear purchases from associated suppliers.
Resale Price Method for distribution and e-commerce intermediary functions.
Cost Plus Method for contract fulfillment and logistics services.
TNMM - Transactional Net Margin Method for benchmarking the net margin of the tested party distributing outdoor equipment.
Profit Split Method for integrated e-commerce value chains combining brand, software, and buyer data.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's economic substance doctrine is embodied in Law 254 of 2021 and DGI Resolution No. 2021-72. Any Panamanian entity deriving relevant income from distribution, services, intellectual property, financing, or insurance must maintain adequate premises, staff, expenditures, and core decision-making in Panama. For a PIF conducting cross-border e-commerce of outdoor camping equipment, the relevant activities are generally foreign-source and therefore not subject to Panamanian tax, but the foundation must still demonstrate real governance by holding board meetings, keeping minutes, maintaining proper books, and controlling its Stripe and PayPal merchant accounts from or through Panama. Mere use of a Panamanian registered address without substance will be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a nil Form 20 while the foundation actually maintains a Panamanian fulfillment center, local delivery personnel, or sales staff, or intentionally omitting Panamanian-source online retail receipts processed through Stripe or PayPal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may assess the omitted tax plus monthly moratory interest and a 10% late-payment surcharge. Criminal tax fraud under the Codigo Fiscal and Codigo Penal carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a monetary fine of at least twice the tax evaded; the foundation's RUC is suspended and the entity is reported on the public in-arrears list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, signatories, and the resident agent are jointly and severally liable for the omitted tax and interest if they knew or should have known of the under-declaration. The Tax Administrative Court may issue travel bans and asset seizure orders, and the corporate veil may be pierced when the PIF is shown to be a mere instrumentality of the director or founder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF solely as a mailing address and receiving foreign e-commerce income without real management, personnel, physical premises, accounting records, board meetings, or independent control over payment and bank accounts, while relying on Panama's territorial tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2021 and DGI Resolution No. 2021-72, the DGI may recharacterize income as Panamanian-source, assess 25% corporate tax plus adjustment penalties up to the full tax omitted, reverse treaty benefits, and dissolve the foundation through the Public Registry for continued non-compliance with annual fees and economic substance declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, fiduciaries, and the resident agent may be subject to civil restitution for all taxes, interest, and penalties. The authorities may impose judicial seizures against personal assets and prohibit the directors from serving as resident agents or officers on any other Panamanian regulated entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF's Stripe and PayPal accounts to receive retail payments and then rapidly transferring funds to personal beneficiary accounts or converting them into crypto assets without customer due diligence, source-of-funds records, or suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) may impose administrative fines up to B/.1,000,000 under Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019. Predicate money-laundering offenses under the Codigo Penal carry imprisonment of 5 to 10 years plus forfeiture of all tainted assets and closure of the relevant merchant accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and any appointed compliance officer face individual criminal prosecution, separate administrative penalties, remand, and travel interdiction. Regulatory cooperation permits freezing orders against bank and PSP accounts plus asset recovery actions against directors who controlled the payment infrastructure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Breach on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing Panamanian-source profits to beneficiaries without applying the statutory 5% or 10% dividend withholding tax, or paying royalties on a brand or software license to a related foreign IP company without the 12.5% royalty withholding and the required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may charge the unwithheld tax, monthly moratory interest, and a penalty of 100% of the amount that should have been withheld. Royalty deductions claimed by the PIF will be disallowed, and any related DTA benefit will be revoked for the tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director or fiduciary who ordered or authorized the distribution or royalty payment without proper withholding becomes personally liable for the full withheld amount, interest, and penalty. If the foreign recipient is a related shell, the ultimate beneficial owner is identified through the beneficial-ownership register and prosecuted jointly with the directors.
